title: "Set scores"
format:

---

singscore (Foroutan et al. 2018) gives every biopsy one score per gene set. Within a biopsy, it
ranks all genes by abundance and averages the ranks of the set's members. A set whose members sit
high in that biopsy scores high. The score depends only on ranks inside one biopsy, so it does not
move when other biopsies are added or removed. This step computes scores and describes them; it
tests nothing.

## Packages

singscore is called with `::` where used.

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "workbooks.R"))
inputs <- c(
  gene_sets = "01_Processing/04_Gene_Sets/c_data/gene_sets.rds",
  proteins = "01_Processing/03_Blood_Correction/c_data/proteins_corrected.rds"
)
paths <- vapply(inputs, here, character(1))
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))
```

## Inputs

Ranking needs every protein in every biopsy and cannot carry a covariate, so the input is limpa's
complete matrix with each protein's blood slope removed from its observed values
(`proteins_corrected.rds`, from `03_Blood_Correction`). Values limpa estimated from the detection
curve are unchanged there.

```{r}
#| label: inputs
gs <- readRDS(paths[["gene_sets"]])
proteins <- readRDS(paths[["proteins"]])
targets <- proteins$targets
c(sets = length(gs$sets), proteins = nrow(proteins), biopsies = ncol(proteins))
```

Sets are keyed on gene symbols, so the matrix rows switch from accessions to the representative
gene chosen in `04_Gene_Sets`.

```{r}
#| label: gene-matrix
gene_map <- filter(gs$protein_map, selected)
stopifnot(all(gene_map$uniprot_id %in% rownames(proteins)), !anyDuplicated(gene_map$gene))
gene_matrix <- proteins$E[gene_map$uniprot_id, ]
rownames(gene_matrix) <- gene_map$gene
dim(gene_matrix)
round(gene_matrix[1:3, 1:3], 2)
```

## Scores

`rankGenes()` ranks genes within each biopsy. `multiScore()` scores every set in one pass and also
returns each set's dispersion: the spread (median absolute deviation) of its members' ranks within
a biopsy. Low dispersion means the members sit together; high means they scatter. By default
singscore centres the score so that 0 means the members' average rank equals the biopsy's middle
rank.

```{r}
#| label: score
ranks <- singscore::rankGenes(gene_matrix)
scored <- singscore::multiScore(ranks, upSetColc = gs$sets)
scores <- scored$Scores
stopifnot(
  identical(rownames(scores), names(gs$sets)),
  identical(colnames(scores), targets$sample_id)
)
dim(scores)
round(scores[1:3, 1:4], 3)
```

Spread across sets within a biopsy reflects which genes each set holds. Spread across biopsies
within a set is what later comparisons use. Both are recorded.

```{r}
#| label: score-summary
score_summary <- tibble(
  n_sets = nrow(scores), n_samples = ncol(scores),
  min = round(min(scores), 4), max = round(max(scores), 4),
  mean = round(mean(scores), 4),
  mean_sd_across_sets = round(mean(apply(scores, 2, sd)), 4),
  mean_sd_across_samples = round(mean(apply(scores, 1, sd)), 4)
)
score_summary
```

```{r}
#| label: spread
set_spread <- gs$set_catalog |>
  filter(qualifies) |>
  transmute(set_id, collection) |>
  mutate(
    score = rowMeans(scores[set_id, ]),
    dispersion = rowMeans(scored$Dispersions[set_id, ])
  )
collection_spread <- set_spread |>
  summarise(
    n_sets = n(), median_score = round(median(score), 4),
    median_dispersion = round(median(dispersion), 1), .by = collection
  )
collection_spread
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-dispersion
#| fig-cap: "Each set's mean score against its mean dispersion, averaged over biopsies."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.5
ggplot(set_spread, aes(score, dispersion, colour = collection)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey80") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1))) +
  labs(x = "mean score across biopsies", y = "mean dispersion across biopsies") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-distribution
#| fig-cap: "Every set's score in every biopsy, pooled within each group-by-time cell."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
tibble(group_time = rep(targets$group_time, each = nrow(scores)), score = as.vector(scores)) |>
  ggplot(aes(score, group_time)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "grey85", colour = NA) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.12, outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(x = "singscore", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9)
```

## How much of the score variation is the person

A principal component analysis (PCA) of the score matrix, then a one-way ANOVA of PC1 and PC2 on
the person (`subject`). The subject share is the fraction of each component's variance that person
identity explains. A large share means comparisons of set scores must account for the person.

```{r}
#| label: structure
components <- prcomp(t(scores), scale. = FALSE)
variance <- summary(components)$importance[2, 1:4]
stopifnot(identical(rownames(components$x), targets$sample_id))
subject_share <- vapply(1:2, function(i) {
  terms <- summary(aov(components$x[, i] ~ targets$subject))[[1]]
  terms[1, 2] / sum(terms[, 2])
}, numeric(1))
structure_check <- tibble(
  component = paste0("PC", 1:4),
  variance_explained = round(as.numeric(variance), 3),
  subject_share = c(round(subject_share, 3), NA, NA)
)
structure_check
```

## Validation

```{r}
#| label: validate
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(scores), identical(dim(scores), c(length(gs$sets), ncol(proteins))),
  all(abs(scores) <= 1), setequal(set_spread$set_id, rownames(scores))
)
```

## Summary

`r nrow(scores)` sets were scored in `r ncol(scores)` biopsies. Scores range from
`r round(min(scores), 2)` to `r round(max(scores), 2)`. Person identity explains
`r round(100 * subject_share[1])`% of PC1 and `r round(100 * subject_share[2])`% of PC2.

## Save

`singscore.rds` holds the set-by-biopsy score matrix (`scores`); later set-level comparisons read
it.

```{r}
#| label: save
out <- here("01_Processing", "05_Set_Scores", "c_data")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(list(scores = scores), file.path(out, "singscore.rds"), compress = "xz")
sheets <- list(
  score_summary = score_summary,
  collection_spread = collection_spread,
  set_spread = set_spread,
  structure_check = structure_check,
  set_scores = as_tibble(scores, rownames = "set_id")
)
holds <- c(
  "Range and spread of the score matrix.",
  "Median score and dispersion per collection.",
  "Mean score and dispersion per set across biopsies.",
  "Variance explained by the first four components, and the subject share of PC1 and PC2.",
  "The set by biopsy score matrix, as saved in singscore.rds."
)
write_workbook(sheets, holds, file.path(out, "set_scores.xlsx"), inputs, paths)
```
